subsystems.name: Core Request Pipeline
subsystems.description: The Core Request Pipeline is the orchestration layer that turns a user-facing axios call into a resolved configuration, a dispatched request, and a settled promise. It exists as its own unit so that adapter selection, config merging, header normalization, cancellation, and transform logic are independent of any particular transport, letting XHR, fetch, and Node HTTP plug in behind one API. A call enters through `createInstance` (`lib/axios.js:28`) and the `Axios` class (`lib/core/Axios.js:22`), then `mergeConfig` (`lib/core/mergeConfig.js:28`) and `transformData` (`lib/core/transformData.js:15`) prepare the request before `dispatchRequest` (`lib/core/dispatchRequest.js:34`) asks `getAdapter` (`lib/adapters/adapters.js:65`) for the environment's transport. Cancellation flows through `CancelToken` (`lib/cancel/CancelToken.js:12`) and `isCancel` (`lib/cancel/isCancel.js:3`), while `AxiosHeaders` (`lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:198`) owns header mutation and serialization. It connects outward to `lib/adapters/fetch.js`, `lib/adapters/http.js`, and `lib/core/AxiosError.js`, and its public entry in `index.js` calls back into `createInstance`.

subsystems.name: HTTP Networking Layer
subsystems.description: The HTTP Networking Layer is the Node.js adapter that performs real socket-level HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 requests after the core pipeline has selected an adapter. It is a separate subsystem because transport concerns—proxying, redirects, TLS, compression, streaming, and FormData encoding—are completely different on Node than in browsers, and isolating them keeps the rest of axios platform-neutral. `resolveConfig` (`lib/helpers/resolveConfig.js:25`) prepares the final config, while the adapter in `lib/adapters/http.js` chooses proxy behavior through `setProxy` (`lib/adapters/http.js:258`) and can switch to `http2Transport` (`lib/adapters/http.js:466`) when HTTP/2 is enabled. Streaming bodies and multipart data are built by `formDataToStream` (`lib/helpers/formDataToStream.js:68`) and `ZlibHeaderTransformStream` (`lib/helpers/ZlibHeaderTransformStream.js:5`), and proxy bypass decisions are made by `shouldBypassProxy` (`lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js:274`). URL building (`lib/helpers/buildURL.js:31`) and data-URI decoding (`lib/helpers/fromDataURI.js:21`) support the adapter's input handling. It connects to `lib/adapters/adapters.js`, `lib/core/Axios.js`, `lib/core/AxiosError.js`, and `lib/core/settle.js`, and is exercised by `tests/unit/adapters/http.test.js`.

subsystems.name: Build and Test Infrastructure
subsystems.description: The Build and Test Infrastructure subsystem contains the tooling that packages, serves, and validates axios during development and CI. It is split from runtime code because build orchestration, sandbox pages, fake XMLHttpRequest implementations, and HTTP test servers should not ship to consumers and would pollute the library's runtime modules. `gulpfile.js` drives the build using `packageJSON` (`gulpfile.js:36`) and `getContributors` (`gulpfile.js:16`), while `tests/setup/server.js` provides shared test servers through `startHTTPServer` (`tests/setup/server.js:20`) and `startTestServer` (`tests/setup/server.js:208`). Browser suites such as `tests/browser/adapter.browser.test.js` and `tests/browser/requests.browser.test.js` inject `MockXMLHttpRequest` classes to simulate XHR behavior, and `tests/unit/adapters/http.test.js` and `tests/unit/adapters/fetch.test.js` cover Node and fetch transports. `sandbox/client.js` and `scripts/axios-build-instance.js` support manual and build-time validation of the produced bundle. It connects to the runtime through `index.js`, `lib/axios.js`, `lib/adapters/fetch.js`, and `lib/adapters/http.js`.

subsystems.name: Shared Utilities
subsystems.description: The Shared Utilities subsystem is a collection of small, dependency-free helpers that the core pipeline, adapters, and public API all rely on. It exists as a distinct unit to centralize common object, function, and stream operations so behavior such as deep merging, type detection, and interceptor bookkeeping is implemented once instead of duplicated across transport layers. `InterceptorManager` (`lib/core/InterceptorManager.js:34`) maintains the request/response interceptor chains, while `lib/utils.js` provides foundational functions like `merge` (`lib/utils.js:461`), `extend` (`lib/utils.js:522`), and `forEach` (`lib/utils.js:371`). Protocol/header helpers such as `parseProtocol` (`lib/helpers/parseProtocol.js:3`) and `parseHeaders` (`lib/helpers/parseHeaders.js:7`) normalize raw inputs, and `bind` (`lib/helpers/bind.js:10`) and `callbackify` (`lib/helpers/callbackify.js:3`) adapt functions for API callers. `AxiosTransformStream` (`lib/helpers/AxiosTransformStream.js:8`) handles streaming transform chunks for Node. These utilities are imported across `lib/axios.js`, `lib/core/Axios.js`, `lib/core/mergeConfig.js`, `lib/helpers/resolveConfig.js`, and every adapter, making them the shared substrate for the whole request pipeline.

It is separated because fetch has a different streaming, abort, and body-size model than XHR or Node's http module, and the error types need to be centralized so every transport reports failures consistently. `factory` (`lib/adapters/fetch.js:68`) constructs the fetch request, `trackStream` (`lib/helpers/trackStream.js:45`) monitors upload/download progress, and `composeSignals` (`lib/helpers/composeSignals.js:5`) merges user and internal abort signals. `settle` (`lib/core/settle.js:14`) decides resolution or rejection based on `validateStatus`, and failures are represented by `AxiosError` (`lib/core/AxiosError.js:98`), whose `redactConfig` logic scrubs sensitive config fields. `validator` (`lib/helpers/validator.js:81`) asserts config options, while `formDataToJSON` (`lib/helpers/formDataToJSON.js:75`) and `estimateDataURLDecodedBytes` (`lib/helpers/estimateDataURLDecodedBytes.js:148`) support body conversions and size checks. It is selected by `lib/adapters/adapters.js`, invoked from `lib/core/Axios.js`, and tested by `tests/unit/adapters/fetch.test.js`.

subsystems.name: Form Data Serialization
subsystems.description: Form Data Serialization turns arbitrary JavaScript request bodies — nested objects, arrays, primitives, Blobs/Files, and URLSearchParams — into platform-facing FormData or URL-encoded pairs. It exists as its own subsystem because Axios supports browser, Node, and React Native environments, all of which expose different FormData/Blob constructors, so the same body-serialization logic must be able to target whichever implementation is present. The flow starts at `toFormData` (lib/helpers/toFormData.js:94), which uses `build` and `defaultVisitor` to walk the object, applies key shaping via `renderKey`/`removeBrackets`, and appends leaves to a native FormData or to an `AxiosURLSearchParams` instance. `toURLEncodedForm` (lib/helpers/toURLEncodedForm.js:7) is the small adapter that chooses the latter for URL-encoded bodies, and the platform index files select the correct Blob/FormData/URLSearchParams classes at runtime. This subsystem is invoked by `lib/defaults/index.js` during transformRequest, is paired with `lib/helpers/formDataToJSON.js` for the inverse conversion, and shares error reporting with `lib/core/AxiosError.js`; `lib/platform/index.js` resolves its browser/node platform exports while `lib/utils.js` supplies the type checks these serializers rely on.

subsystems.name: URL Path Utilities
subsystems.description: URL Path Utilities resolve the final request URL from a configured `baseURL` and a per-request `requestedURL`. It exists as a separate subsystem because URL joining involves several non-trivial concerns — trailing/leading slashes, absolute-URL detection, protocol validation, and sanitization of sensitive fragments — that should not be duplicated by the HTTP, XHR, and fetch adapters. `buildFullPath` (lib/core/buildFullPath.js:68) is the entry point: it calls `combineURLs` to join segments, `isAbsoluteURL` to detect absolute targets, and `assertValidHttpProtocolURL`/`redactSensitiveURLParts` to reject or scrub malformed URLs before returning the final path. `normalizeURLForProtocolCheck` is used as a preprocessor for the protocol checks. The subsystem connects outward to `lib/adapters/xhr.js`, `lib/adapters/http.js`, and `lib/core/Axios.js`, which all call `buildFullPath` when dispatching requests, and it uses `lib/core/AxiosError.js` to surface invalid-URL failures; `lib/helpers/resolveConfig.js` ties the resolved config into this path-building step.

subsystems.name: Progress Event Helpers
subsystems.description: Progress Event Helpers supply a uniform progress-reporting layer on top of the different event models of XMLHttpRequest, fetch, and Node streams. It is split out so each adapter can call the same reducers/decorators instead of reimplementing throttling, speed estimation, and progress-callback normalization. `progressEventReducer` (lib/helpers/progressEventReducer.js:5) builds a listener that feeds raw loaded/total values through `speedometer` (lib/helpers/speedometer.js:9) and invokes the user callback with computed rate/estimated fields; `progressEventDecorator` and `asyncDecorator` adapt that listener to streamed or promise-based adapters. `throttle` (lib/helpers/throttle.js:7) provides the interval-based pacing used by the reducer so callbacks do not fire on every chunk. It is consumed directly by `lib/adapters/xhr.js`, `lib/adapters/http.js`, and `lib/adapters/fetch.js`, with `lib/utils.js` providing shared utilities such as warning/type helpers.

subsystems.name: Rollup Build Config
subsystems.description: Rollup Build Config is the repository's distribution-bundling subsystem: it turns the lib source tree into the published ESM, CJS, and UMD artifacts. It is separate because the packaging matrix (input entries, output file names, Node builtin externalization, minification) is orthogonal to runtime source code and would otherwise clutter package scripts. Rollup loads `rollup.config.js`, then `build` (rollup.config.js:25) collects `buildConfig` (rollup.config.js:18) results for each target, while `nodeCjsExternal` (rollup.config.js:67) decides which Node built-ins are left external for CJS bundles. The constants near the top of the file — `lib`, `outputFileName`, `name`, `namedInput`, and `defaultInput` — parameterize each generated configuration. Its `related_files` list is empty because it is build tooling rather than a runtime module, but it is tightly coupled to `lib/axios.js` and `package.json` as the source entry and metadata for the published bundles.

files.role: Rollup configuration that defines how the source tree is packaged into distributable ESM, CJS, and UMD bundles. It owns the build matrix, so source modules never need environment-specific packaging directives.

subsystems.name: ESLint Configuration
subsystems.description: ESLint Configuration is the repository's linting policy, expressed in the modern flat-config format used by ESLint v9+. It exists as its own item so style and error rules are centralized and easy to adjust without touching source files or package scripts. When a developer runs the lint command, ESLint loads `eslint.config.js` and applies the exported rule set, language options, and ignore patterns across source, tests, configuration, and build files. Because its `related_files` list is empty, it has no runtime imports or execution path; it only constrains how every other subsystem is written during development.

files.role: Flat ESLint configuration exporting the repository's lint rules, language options, and ignore patterns. ESLint loads it automatically during lint runs.

subsystems.name: TypeScript Definitions
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the TypeScript definition surface for the axios API, exposing request configuration, headers, responses, errors, interceptors, and cancellation types through index.d.ts. It exists as a separate unit because type declarations must be consumable by the TypeScript compiler and editors without pulling in runtime JavaScript, giving axios a typed contract for users while keeping the implementation untyped. Data flows through the public types when a user calls methods on AxiosInstance (index.d.ts:710) or AxiosStatic (index.d.ts:766); the compiler resolves options against AxiosRequestConfig (index.d.ts:391) and headers against AxiosHeaders (index.d.ts:25). Runtime values such as Axios (index.d.ts:646), AxiosError (index.d.ts:524), and CanceledError (index.d.ts:566) are declared so that imported objects have usable shapes, while helper and option types like MethodsHeaders (index.d.ts:12), ContentType (index.d.ts:113), and ResponseType (index.d.ts:272) constrain individual configuration fields. The scan lists no related files for this subsystem, so its direct neighbour is the package TypeScript entry point that re-exports these declarations to consumers.

files.role: Declares the public TypeScript surface for axios, including request/response types, header classes, error classes, and interceptor managers. It is the file TypeScript users compile against, while runtime implementation stays in the JavaScript lib tree.

subsystems.name: Environment FormData
subsystems.description: This subsystem isolates the FormData implementation for the current runtime in lib/env/classes/FormData.js. It exists as a separate environment module because Node.js and browsers have different native FormData behaviors, and axios needs one import site that can be swapped or adapted without changing core serialization logic. Data and control flow occur when a request needs multipart encoding: the FormData class from this module is instantiated and used to build the payload that is then handed to the platform transport. Because the scan recorded no key symbols and no related files for this subsystem, its real connections are through the environment abstraction layer and the core helpers that import the class for FormData-based requests.

files.role: Provides an environment-specific FormData class that axios can instantiate when building multipart payloads. It isolates platform differences so core serialization code does not need to know whether it is running in a browser or in Node.

subsystems.name: Deprecated Method Helper
subsystems.description: This subsystem is a tiny helper that centralizes axios's deprecation warnings through the deprecatedMethod function in lib/helpers/deprecatedMethod.js. It exists as a separate unit so that every call site wanting to mark an old API as deprecated can share the same warning message format and emit behavior, rather than duplicating warning logic across the codebase. Control flow starts when legacy code paths invoke deprecatedMethod (lib/helpers/deprecatedMethod.js:15), and the helper carries out the warning behavior before the caller continues. The scan records no related files for this helper, so its neighbours are whichever modules import it at call sites; it is primarily connected to the helper layer and to deprecated axios entry points.

files.role: Implements the deprecatedMethod helper used to warn about obsolete axios APIs. Keeping it in its own file lets any deprecated call site reuse identical warning behavior.

key_symbols.name: deprecatedMethod

subsystems.name: Null Helper
subsystems.description: This subsystem provides an explicit null value as a module export from lib/helpers/null.js. It exists as a separate unit because axios needs a stable, importable null sentinel to represent no value in places where undefined or an empty implementation could cause ambiguous behavior in defaults or transformation chains. Control flow is simple: when a module imports this file, it receives the same null value and can place it into arrays, objects, or option defaults. The scan lists no key symbols or related files, so no concrete neighbour connections can be named; it is a leaf module available to the rest of the helper layer.

files.role: Exports a standalone null sentinel for use as a no-op default value. Having null as an importable module makes it easy for other helper files to reference a consistent empty value without hard-coding null in multiple branches.

subsystems.name: Sandbox Server
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the Node HTTP server used by axios's sandbox test environment, implemented in sandbox/server.js. It exists separately from the library so developers can exercise axios against a local controlled server without shipping test infrastructure in the package. Control flow begins when the server receives an HTTP request: requestHandler (sandbox/server.js:75) decides whether the request targets an API route or a static file, delegates API calls to handleApiRequest (sandbox/server.js:33), and serves files through pipeFileToResponse (sandbox/server.js:14); the server listens on the PORT constant (sandbox/server.js:111). The scan records no related files for this subsystem, but the sandbox pages it serves are the neighbouring client code that connects to it during manual testing.

files.role: Runs the local sandbox HTTP server used for manually exercising axios against realistic requests. It serves static assets and exposes API endpoints that mirror common backend scenarios.

subsystems.name: Vitest Configuration
subsystems.description: The Vitest Configuration subsystem centralises settings for running the project's test suite with Vitest. It exists as its own unit so test-runner options, environment setup, and coverage rules do not leak into application or build code and can be changed without touching source files. When vitest is launched, it reads vitest.config.js at the project root and applies the options defined there to the test environment. Test discovery and execution then follow those settings, including which files are treated as tests and how they are transformed. The subsystem has no related_files, so it is a standalone configuration point rather than an importable module; its only consumer is the Vitest CLI.

files.role: vitest.config.js is the single configuration entry point for the Vitest test runner. It is loaded by Vitest during startup and supplies the resolver, environment, and coverage settings used to execute the test suite.

subsystems.name: Webpack Configuration
subsystems.description: The Webpack Configuration subsystem defines how the project is bundled for development and production builds. It exists separately to keep build tooling isolated from application logic, allowing bundle entry points, loaders, plugins, and output paths to be managed in one place. The generateConfig function in webpack.config.js produces the configuration object that webpack consumes; when the CLI starts a build, it invokes this function and uses the returned object to control module resolution and output. Because related_files is empty, the config does not import or get imported by other subsystems, functioning purely as the build-time instruction set for webpack.

files.role: webpack.config.js holds the build configuration for webpack. Its generateConfig function assembles the options webpack needs to resolve modules, apply loaders, and write output bundles.

key_symbols.name: generateConfig

overview.description: The system is an HTTP client library that routes user requests through a core pipeline, which merges configuration, normalizes headers, applies transforms, and dispatches to an environment-appropriate adapter. The request flow draws on shared utilities for interceptors, merging, and type checks; URL path utilities to build the final URL; form-data serialization to encode bodies; and progress event helpers to report upload/download progress uniformly across transports. The transport layer is realized by the Node HTTP networking adapter and the fetch adapter, both producing AxiosError-shaped outcomes, while environment-specific FormData is isolated and cancellation, header, and error logic is owned by the core. Around this runtime sit a TypeScript type surface and build/test subsystems such as Rollup, webpack, ESLint, Vitest, and a sandbox server that package, lint, and validate the code without shipping as runtime modules.
